end.summary:
- Practised linking webbed duck feet to swimming and chicken feet to walking and scratching.
- Practised matching bird beaks with foods: kingfisher–fish, sparrow–seeds, eagle–meat; still building beak/foot links.
- Practised sorting living and non-living things; some answers were right, but the plant mix-up was not corrected after it appeared again.
- Practised linking leaf features to plant habitats; some answers were right, with more checking needed next time.
end.parentNote: Atharv practised observing bird feet, beaks, plants, and living things by giving reasons from their shapes and actions. They connected webbed feet with swimming and identified several bird foods; the method of using clues was useful. They still mixed up whether plants are living because they do not move or eat like animals, and this was not corrected after the last time it appeared. At home, ask Atharv to find one plant and one non-living object, then name one sign that shows whether each is living.
